Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- The failing test FastDateParserTest.testLANG_831 expects SimpleDateFormat (SDF) and FastDateParser (FDP) to behave the same for pattern "M E" and date string "3  Tue" (note: two spaces). With shouldFail = true, both parsers should reject the input because the pattern contains exactly one space, but the input has two.
  - Test snippet:
    - testLANG_831: testSdfAndFdp("M E","3  Tue", true)
    - Helper: testSdfAndFdp(...) tries SDF and FDF, expecting both to throw; if either succeeds, it fails the test.

- SDF behavior: In SimpleDateFormat, a literal space in the pattern must match exactly one space in the input; extra whitespace causes a parse failure. Thus SDF rightly fails on "3  Tue" for "M E".

- FDP behavior: FastDateParser builds a regex from the pattern in init():
  - It tokenizes the pattern using formatPattern (lines 535–536): the regex includes a branch for non-letter runs "[^'A-Za-z]++", which will capture the literal space between M and E as a separate token.
  - In init() (lines 120–149), each token is converted to a regex fragment via Strategy.addRegex(this, regex). The literal, non-letter token (the single space) is handled by a “literal/copy” strategy (e.g., CopyQuotedStrategy).
  - Per the issue report and the observed behavior, that strategy expands any whitespace in the pattern to a regex that matches variable-length whitespace (e.g., \s*+ or \s+), instead of matching the literal characters exactly.
  - Consequently, the generated overall regex for "M E" allows any amount of whitespace between month and day-of-week, so the input "3  Tue" (two spaces) is accepted by FDP.

- Why the test fails:
  - SDF throws an exception (as expected) because the input has two spaces where the pattern has one.
  - FDP parses successfully because the literal space in the pattern was turned into a flexible whitespace matcher, contrary to SDF’s exact matching rules.
  - The test then fails on the expectation that both should fail:
    - Either at “Expected FDF failure, but got …” if FDP returns a Date, or at the subsequent assertion that both or neither should throw.

- Root cause:
  - The strategy that handles literal/non-letter pattern tokens expands whitespace in the pattern into a regex that matches any amount of whitespace, rather than matching the literal number and type of whitespace characters present in the pattern.
  - This diverges from SimpleDateFormat’s behavior and leads to FDP accepting inputs SDF rejects, exactly as described in the current bug report (“FastDateParser does not handle white-space properly”).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
